scenario: AiTA for not trusting a delivery driver? | Today I ordered food off of an app- it's a third party delivery service that picks up the food and delivers your order. Once you pay online, you're given a code that you give to the delivery driver once he gives you your food (I assume that's how the drivers get paid). The app generates a time that you can expect to get your food by, and the drivers are expected to complete the delivery by then, so if you don't get your order by the promised time you often get a percentage of your order cost refunded. Drivers are not limited in how many orders they can pick up simultaneously (they use their discretion to pick up the tickets they want), but if they take too many at once, they will exceed the time limit and most likely suffer a penalty. ​ I had ordered one tea and 2 pastries, for which I only received one. I called the shop and the manager was very apologetic, offering to using the service to send me out the missing pastry ASAP. I had assumed they would just refund me through the app, but that solution was fine too. The shop paid the delivery fee, and I was given the code to give to the driver when my order arrived. About twenty minutes later, the driver called me to ask for the code, stating he was on his way. I thanked him for letting me know he was coming and hung up, to which he called back two minutes later asking for the code again. I replied that I would have it for him the minute he arrived. After another two minutes, he called back again telling me he was nearby and he was running out of time, could he have the code? I told him he would get the code when I got my food. This time I was a bit annoyed, as he knows the rules as a driver and the only way I can guarantee that my food will be delivered is to hold onto the code until my food is here. The guy snapped at me: do you not understand the code is about to expire?! And I retorted back: Well, you better hurry then, right? as nicely as possible before hanging up. I didn't want to argue any longer, but I wasn't about to risk not getting my item by giving up the code. My friend told me that I was being selfish and unkind since the guy might not get paid for the delivery. I argued that since he voluntarily picked up the ticket, he shouldn't have taken ones he couldn't deliver on time. He said something to the effect of, "thank goodness the world isn't full of unkind bitches like you". ​ So, AItA? Should I have just given him the code and trusted he would still bring me my food? ​ The end of the story is, after I refused to tell him the code, I never heard from him again nor did I see my pastry. The shop manager saw the order wasn't marked as delivered and called to ask what happened, to which I told her the details. She tried to call the delivery guy then, but he had turned off his phone, so she apologized profusely, refunded me through the app, and reported him to the delivery service management. The manager said that he will either be severely disciplined or fired over this.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the person in this scenario did the right thing by not giving the delivery driver the code. Let me break it down step by step. First, the setup: They ordered food through an app, which uses third-party delivery drivers. The payment is handled via a code given to the driver upon delivery. If the driver doesn't deliver on time, they might get penalized, but they can choose how many orders to take. The person ordered one tea and two pastries but only received one. The shop manager apologized and offered to send the missing pastry, and the shop covered the delivery fee, giving the person the code. Then, the driver called multiple times asking for the code, even before arriving. The person was hesitant to give the code until they received the food, which led to an argument. The driver snapped at them, and they responded by telling the driver to hurry. The driver didn't deliver, and the shop refunded them and reported the driver. The friend thinks the person was being unkind and selfish, arguing that the driver might not get paid. The person counters that the driver shouldn't have taken the order if they couldn't deliver on time. So, the question is: Should the person have given the code to the driver, trusting they'd deliver, or was it justified to hold onto it? Let me consider the rules of the service. The code is given upon delivery, which makes sense because it's the driver's proof of delivery. If the person gives the code before receiving the food, they have no guarantee the driver will actually deliver. The driver could take the code and not bring the food, leaving the person without their order and without recourse. The driver called multiple times, which might indicate they were in a rush or had other issues. The person was within their rights to wait for the food before giving the code. It's a mutual agreement: the driver delivers, the person gives the code. Without the code, the driver doesn't get paid, but that's the system in place to ensure delivery. The friend's argument is that the person was unkind, but kindness shouldn't override the system's rules. The person wasn't being unkind; they were following the process to ensure they received their order. The driver, on the other hand, was pressuring the person to give the code before delivery, which is against the system's design. Additionally, the driver's behavior was unprofessional. They snapped at the person, which isn't acceptable. The person handled the situation calmly and rationally, even when provoked. In the end, the shop refunded the person and reported the driver, which suggests that the system supports the customer's right to withhold the code until delivery. The driver's actions led to their potential discipline or firing, which is a consequence of not following the rules. So, considering all this, the person did the right thing by not giving the code until they received the food. They were protecting their own interests and following the established process, which ultimately led to a resolution where they were refunded and the driver faced consequences for their actions.
